Problem: MacroMicroPicker label is static — grid feels like a form extracting data, not a dialogue offering language
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Gallup: 3.6T lost to disengagement. Polya lower aims: employee learned for livelihood, already hates forms from bad school. A form says "the system needs data from you." A conversation says "let me help you name what happened." Recognition over recall only works if the FRAMING is recognition too — currently the label is a command, not a question that adapts.
What Employee Experiences: Employee sees "What would have enabled better performance?" then 5 pills. Picks Talent. Same label stays. Picks Key-person dependency. No response. Next screen. Feels like a test with no feedback — the same pattern that made them hate school.
Fix: Make label dynamic with 3 states. Pre-selection: "Something got in the way today. What area?" After macro (Talent): "What about talent specifically?" After micro (Key-person dependency): "Key-person dependency — got it." Three label props on MacroMicroPicker: label, microPrompt (keyed by macroId), confirmationTemplate. Data collected is identical. Experience is a dialogue.

Problem: 7 vectors across 7 screens feels long even though each pick is 5 seconds — perception problem not time problem
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman Gulf of Execution: "can the user figure out how to do what they want?" The user wants to FINISH. 7 screens with no narrative connective tissue feels like 7 separate forms. The 3-act structure is right but the transitions between acts are page-boundaries not story-beats. Polya: good pedagogy sequences experiences so each builds on the last — isolated screens dont build.
What Employee Experiences: Employee toggles deliverables (Act 1). Clicks Next. New screen with pills (Act 2). Clicks Next. Another screen with pills (Act 3). Three disconnected forms. No sense of "I'm telling one story." No sense of progress within Act 2 (3 sub-steps, progress bar shows 100% immediately).
Fix: Two fixes: (A) Bridge texts between acts create narrative momentum. Act1→2: "[n] not done — what got in the way?" (already exists, strengthen). Act2→3: "You navigated it. Now — how are you?" (missing, add). (B) Progress bar shows sub-step fill within Act 2: tapping=33%, voice=66%, confirm=100%. Together these make 3 forms feel like 1 story in 3 beats.

Lens: Norman P3: Feedback After Not During
Problem: All feedback (streak, points, patterns) comes at end in SummaryCard. Nothing during the picking. Employee fills → gets reward. Skinner box, not mirror.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Goldratt: "Tell me how you measure me and I will tell you how I will behave." If reward comes only at the end, employee optimizes for speed-to-completion, not quality-of-reflection. Polya higher aims: learning to exploit inner talent requires SEEING your own patterns. Seeing happens when the mirror appears while youre still looking — not after you walk away. The daily report should be the mirror that makes the employee see themselves as a capable navigator, not a data-entry clerk who gets a streak badge.
What Employee Experiences: Employee picks constraint micro. Nothing. Picks navigation micro. Nothing. Records voice. Nothing. Picks framework. Nothing. Picks feeling. Nothing. Submits. NOW gets streak + points + patterns. The 60 seconds of picking were a chore. The 5 seconds of feedback were the reward. Ratio is wrong.
Fix:
Inline feedback at two moments during the flow: (A) After constraint micro: single

below pills — "3rd time this week — this one's persistent." Shows only when real history exists. No placeholder. (B) After feeling micro: "You've felt this on days with Internal Support constraints." Connects feeling to cause. These are mirrors not rewards. Employee thinks "huh, it IS the third time" — thats the beginning of TOC thinking without knowing the term. Implementation: AnimatePresence, one line, data from backend history API.

Problem: The 5x5 grids are not constraints on the employee — they are shared language that makes patterns detectable by both the system AND the employee
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Without grid: employee says "Bob was busy" Monday, "waiting on Bob" Wednesday, "couldnt proceed without Bobs input" Friday — 3 free-text entries no system can cluster. With grid: "Key-person dependency" 3 times — pattern is visible because VOCABULARY is stable. Goldratt: the grid is the Drum (sets vocabulary pace), daily repetition is the Rope (pulls employee through thinking process), feedback signals are the Buffer (protect learning from being forgotten between days). Polya: higher aims need stable conceptual vocabulary — you cant develop expertise without naming things consistently.
What Employee Experiences: Days 1-7: picks mechanically, habit forming. Days 8-14: inline feedback appears, employee notices THEIR OWN pattern. Days 15-30: starts anticipating constraint pick before opening app — classifying in real-time during meetings. Days 30-60: notices navigation variety, tries new approaches consciously. Days 60-90: IS a TOC practitioner. Never read The Goal. Grid was the teacher.
Fix: This is not a fix — it is a DESIGN VALIDATION. The grids stay. The 5x5 stays. The question-answer rhythm (N1), inline feedback (N3), and bridge texts (N2) make the grids feel like a conversation instead of a test. Do NOT replace grids with free text. Do NOT reduce grid options. The grids ARE the curriculum.
File(s): All MacroMicroPicker usages — preserve grid architecture

Problem: When constraint auto-highlights paired navigation macro, the pairing rationale is invisible. Employee doesnt know WHY that navigation is highlighted.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Goldratt Five Focusing Steps: Identify constraint → Exploit it → Subordinate. The constraint-navigation pairing IS the identify-exploit link. But the current UI just highlights the paired nav macro with no explanation. The employee doesnt learn that specific constraints have specific exploitation strategies. The pairing is the most powerful teaching mechanism in the entire flow and its silent.
What Employee Experiences: Employee picks Talent > Key-person dependency. Navigation section: "Pair or train" macro pill glows primary/50. Employee thinks "why is that one highlighted?" Picks it because it glows. Picks a micro. Moves on. Never understood the pairing. Learning opportunity wasted.
Fix: Add bridging line between constraint completion and navigation section: "People who hit [Key-person dependency] often try..." then navigation macros with paired one highlighted. Single sentence. Teaches the constraint→exploitation link organically. Employee absorbs TOC without studying it.

Problem: Report measures busyness (task count) not throughput (which deliverable moved the constraint). Employee marks 3/3 done and feels great even if none were on critical chain. "Done" measures activity on the item, not whether the program constraint moved. done + not_done is insufficient — need quality signal on critical path items.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Goldratt: improving anything that is NOT the bottleneck is an illusion of progress. If daily report only captures done/partial/not_done, it rewards local optima. "Done" conflates activity with output — employee could spend 2h on API Integration, mark done, and the actual bottleneck (API team deploying their end) is still blocked. Output = did completing this item change the state of the program constraint? That requires a quality signal, not just a completion toggle. Polya: higher aims = learning to distinguish essential from incidental AND learning to evaluate quality of own work against specs.
What Employee Experiences: Employee toggles all 3 deliverables to done. Tension summary shows 3 done 0h gap. Feels productive. But 2 of 3 were non-critical busywork. Critical path item is "done" but QA specs werent met — output is zero. Report celebrated the wrong thing with the wrong measure.
Fix: Three-layer fix across plan and report: (A) PLAN PHASE: employee/PM marks which items are on critical path. Plan view shows a chokepoint map (Strait of Hormuz metaphor) — non-critical items are wide open lanes, critical path item is a narrow passage all progress funnels through. Builds tension visually before the day starts. (B) REPORT ACT 1: items arrive pre-sorted from plan, critical path on top with visual weight. Quick toggle to promote/demote a normal item to critical path (priorities shift during the day). Critical path items get a 5-state QA spec toggle instead of simple done/partial/not_done: qa_unknown ("QA specs unknown" — nobody defined quality bar), qa_met ("QA specs met" — work meets criteria), qa_to_verify ("QA specs to be verified" — work done, not yet checked), qa_unsure ("Not sure" — employee doesnt know), qa_not_met ("QA specs not met" — done but below bar). Non-critical items keep simple done/partial/not_done. (C) ACT 2 BRANCHING: QA status drives constraint framing — qa_met: "What almost got in the way?", qa_not_met: "What blocked quality?", qa_unknown: "What would the spec even look like?", qa_to_verify/qa_unsure: "Anything that might affect verification?" (D) TENSION SUMMARY: shows critical path QA status at top of hierarchy, separate from non-critical done/partial/notDone counts. (E) SUMMARY/ECHO: reflects critical path item + QA status. "Done + QA met" = real output signal. "Done + QA not met" = activity without output. "Done + QA unknown" = quality bar undefined (itself a problem worth surfacing).
File(s): v6/data/types.ts (add QaCriticalPathStatus type, add to PlannedDeliverable) + v6/Act1Work/Act1Work.tsx (QA toggle for critical path items, quick promote/demote) + v5/ToggleList.tsx (QA spec toggle UI for critical path items, keep done/partial/not_done for non-critical) + v6/Act2Story/Act2Story.tsx (branch framing on QA status) + v6/Act1Work/TensionSummary.tsx (critical path QA at top of hierarchy) + v6/SummaryCard.tsx (echo critical path + QA) + v6/DailyReportV6.tsx (echo screen) + plan-phase components (chokepoint map, Strait of Hormuz visual)

Problem: Everything flowed? Skip produces zero constraint signal for that day. If 30%+ skip, the feedback loop breaks. The drum goes silent.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Goldratt: there is ALWAYS a constraint. "Everything flowed" means the constraint was invisible, not absent. A smooth day has a POSITIVE constraint — what went right? That signal is equally valuable for exploitation. Polya: even a student who aced the test should reflect on what enabled it — thats how expertise compounds.
What Employee Experiences: Employee had a smooth day. Clicks "Everything flowed? Skip." Goes to Act 3. Zero constraint signal captured. Pattern detection for that day: blank. Over time, smooth days become data voids. Program manager cant distinguish "smooth" from "employee didnt bother."
Fix: Rename to "No major blockers today." When tapped, show ONE question: "What made today smooth?" (text input, max 100 chars). Store as smoothDayNote in ReportState. This captures positive constraint signal. The drum keeps beating even on good days. Add smoothDayNote: string to ReportState.

Lens: Goldratt: Streak Rewards Submission Not Quality
Problem: Streak gamification rewards showing up, not signal quality. Employee can click through minimum path in 30 seconds and maintain streak. Incentive misalignment.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Goldratt: "Tell me how you measure me and I will tell you how I will behave." If streak is the hero metric, employee optimizes for daily completion speed. A skip-through with random picks = same streak as a thoughtful 90-second reflection. The measurement drives the wrong behavior. Polya: lower aims produce lower engagement — if the reward is just "I did it" not "I learned something" then the ritual becomes mechanical.
What Employee Experiences: Employee in a rush. Taps done-done-done, skips Act 2, picks random framework, picks random feeling, submits. "8-day streak!" Same reward as the employee who reflected carefully. Over time, the careful employee sees no difference and starts rushing too. Race to the bottom.
Fix: Add signal strength indicator alongside streak. Compute from report completeness: constraint + narrative + specific detail = Strong. Constraint but no narrative = Moderate. Skip-through = Weak. Display: "Signal: Strong" with colored indicator next to streak badge. This shifts incentive from submission frequency to reflection quality without punishing — weak signal still counts for streak, but the employee sees the difference.

Problem: TimeStepper minus buttons dont work. Adapter hardcodes actualMins: 0 so minus is always disabled (minutes <= 0). handleAdjustTime writes to estimateMins (budget) instead of actualMins.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman Gulf of Execution: user clicks minus, nothing happens. Norman: "Silence after an action is an error message that was never written." The button LOOKS clickable but is disabled because the underlying data is wrong. This is a Norman Door — the affordance (clickable button) fights the state (always 0). Budget (estimateMins) must be immutable once day starts — its the plan. Actual time is what the employee adjusts.
What Employee Experiences: Employee tries to reduce time on a task they finished quickly. Minus button is greyed out. They can only increase. They think the feature is broken. Trust erodes. They stop using time adjustment entirely. Tension summary never reflects real plan-vs-actual gap because both sides move together.
Fix: (A) Add actualMins: number to PlannedDeliverable type. (B) Add actualMins: 0 to mock data. (C) Fix adapter: actualMins: d.actualMins instead of hardcoded 0. (D) Fix handleAdjustTime to write to d.actualMins not d.estimateMins. (E) Fix tensionSummaryAtom to compute real actualMins from deliverables. (F) Fix TensionSummary to use real delta: totalActual = sum(actualMins) + unplannedMins - sum(estimateMins).
File(s): v6/data/types.ts + v6/data/mockData.ts + v6/data/adapters.ts + v6/Act1Work/Act1Work.tsx + v6/data/atoms.ts + v6/Act1Work/TensionSummary.tsx

Lens: Time Stepper: Layout and Missing Buttons
Problem: Only one minus button (-30m). No -1h. Layout asymmetric. Need: [-1h][-30m] actual/budget [+30m][+1h].
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman mapping principle: relationship between controls and effects must be spatial/logical. Current layout has 1 button left, 2 buttons right. Asymmetry breaks spatial logic. The employee who spent 2 hours less than planned needs 4 clicks of -30m. The +1h exists but -1h doesnt. The control set is biased toward over-reporting.
What Employee Experiences: Employee finished a 2h task in 30 minutes. Needs to reduce by 90 min. Must click -30m three times. No -1h button exists. Tedious. Meanwhile adding time has -30m, +30m AND +1h — 3 options to add, 1 to subtract.
Fix: Symmetric layout: [-1h][-30m] display [+30m][+1h]. Display shows actual/budget (e.g. "30m / 2h"). All 4 buttons: min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]. Add disabled={minutes <= 0} on both minus buttons.

Problem: No visual distinction between actual and budget. Employee cant see at a glance if theyre over, under, or on budget.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman visibility principle: if user cannot see the state, they cannot predict outcome. A number without color is just a number. Red/yellow/green is a universal signal the employee processes instantly without reading. Goldratt: the constraint is visible only when the gap between plan and actual is VISIBLE. Hidden gaps hide constraints.
What Employee Experiences: Employee sees "1h 30m / 2h" but no color. Is that good or bad? They have to do math. At 5:45 PM after a long day, they wont. The tension summary below does this math but per-item color coding gives instant per-task feedback.
Fix: Color the actual value: Red (text-error) when actual > budget — took longer. Yellow (text-warning) when actual === budget — exactly on plan. Green (text-success) when actual < budget — finished faster. Budget stays muted (text-base-content/50). Employee sees green/red per task without thinking.

Problem: handleSummaryDismiss calls freshState() then sets step=done. freshState() nullifies constraint/navigation/framework/feeling. Echo screen reads null. Shows blank celebration.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman feedback loop: action (submit) → system response (summary) → user evaluates → next. The evaluation step (echo screen) is broken — it shows nothing. The employee completed a thoughtful report and the system responds with a blank screen. The ritual ends with silence. Norman: "Silence after an action is an error message that was never written."
What Employee Experiences: Employee submits. SummaryCard shows constraint → navigation, framework x qty, feeling, streak. Taps to dismiss. Echo screen: fire emoji, streak number, but constraint/framework/feeling lines are empty. "See you tomorrow." The story they just told vanished. Feels like the system didnt actually save anything.
Fix: Change handleSummaryDismiss from setState({...freshState(), step: done}) to setState(prev => ({...prev, step: done})). Move freshState() into handleStartNew only. Echo screen then reads the real report data.

Problem: Back from Act 3 goes to act1 when Act 2 was skipped. Employee loses all Act 1 status toggles. Must redo everything.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman Gulf of Execution: "back" should mean "one step back" not "restart." The employee's mental model of Back is spatial — go to the previous screen. Going back 2-3 screens breaks spatial mapping. Polya: frustration from having to redo work = lower-aims pattern. System should protect completed work.
What Employee Experiences: Employee skips Act 2 (smooth day). Enters Act 3. Picks framework. Realizes they want to change a deliverable status. Presses Back. Lands on Act 1. All deliverable statuses preserved (theyre in state) but the employee perceives a restart. If they wanted Act 2 theyd need to go through Act 1 again.
Fix: Change handleBack: always goToStep(act2_tapping) regardless of skippedAct2. From act2_tapping user can re-skip in one tap or go back to act1 themselves. One step back, always.

Problem: Recording restart overwrites entire transcript. onresult replaces narrative each time instead of appending to existing text.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman error prevention: the best error message is one that was never needed. The employee edits their transcript, presses record to add more, and their edits vanish. No undo. No warning. Destructive action with no recovery path. Polya: the reflective student who re-reads and refines their answer should not be punished for it.
What Employee Experiences: Employee records "I was blocked by the API team." Stops. Edits to "I was blocked by the API team all morning." Records again to add more. Entire transcript replaced with the new recording. Edits gone. Employee frustrated, gives up on voice, types minimal text.
Fix: On startRecording: snapshot currentTranscript. In onresult: prepend snapshot with space separator. previousText + " " + newTranscript. Append behavior, not replace.

Problem: Back from StoryConfirmation goes to act2_tapping (constraint picker) instead of act2_voice (where their text is). Jumps back 2 steps.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman mapping: Back should go to the immediately previous screen. Going from confirm → picker skips the voice screen where the employee's content lives. Their narrative is still in state but they dont see it — they see the constraint picker again. Disorienting.
What Employee Experiences: Employee records narrative, moves to confirm, reads it, wants to add a sentence. Presses Back. Lands on constraint/navigation pickers. Their narrative is elsewhere. They have to press forward through the picker again to reach their text.
Fix: Change goToStep(act2_tapping) to goToStep(act2_voice) in StoryConfirmation back button handler.

Problem: SummaryCard disappears after 5 seconds. Streak, points, pattern feedback — the employee wanted to read these.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman: feedback must be perceivable. A 5-second timer on the reward screen creates anxiety not delight. The employee is processing their first gamification signal and it vanishes. Polya: reflection requires time. Rushing the student past their results prevents learning. The summary is where the daily-to-identity connection happens — dont rush it.
What Employee Experiences: Employee submits. Summary slides up. Reads "Day captured." Sees constraint persistence badge. Starts reading streak count. Screen disappears. "Wait, what was my points score?" Gone. Tap anywhere to dismiss was at 30% opacity and they missed it. The one moment of feedback was snatched away.
Fix: Remove setTimeout(onDismiss, 5000). Keep onClick={onDismiss} on backdrop. Employee dismisses when ready.

Problem: Status toggle cycles not_done → done → partial. Most common action (done) requires 2 clicks from null. Partial requires overshooting past done.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman affordance: the first click should produce the most likely desired outcome. Most employees toggle to mark things done. Done should be first in cycle. Polya: the student who succeeds should be rewarded immediately (1 click = done), not forced through failure first (1 click = not_done).
What Employee Experiences: Employee taps a deliverable they finished. Status goes to not_done (red). They wanted done (green). Tap again — done. 2 taps for the most common action. Employee wanting partial must tap through not_done AND done to reach it — 3 taps from null, overshooting done.
Fix: Change CYCLE from [not_done, done, partial] to [done, partial, not_done]. Also update STATUS_CYCLE in report-v5.types.ts if shared.

Problem: canProceedToVoice uses OR — employee can pick only navigation without constraint and proceed. Voice prompt shows "..." for missing label.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman error prevention: if the system needs both constraint and navigation, dont allow proceeding with only one. If only one is needed, dont show "..." as placeholder. Either enforce or communicate. Silent acceptance of incomplete state is a design failure — the employee doesnt know if they did it right. Goldratt: a half-identified constraint is worse than none — it gives false signal.
What Employee Experiences: Employee picks navigation micro but skips constraint. "Tell your story" enables. They proceed. Voice prompt: "You faced ... and used Clarified RACI." The "..." is confusing. Did they miss something? Is the system broken? They proceed anyway. Report has navigation but no constraint. Pattern detection for constraints: blank for that day.
Fix: Make both required: change || to && in canProceedToVoice. The grid is the curriculum — skipping half the lesson breaks the learning sequence.

Problem: Submit button fires goToStep(summary) immediately. No preview of what will be submitted. 5+ screens of selections committed in one tap.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman error prevention: destructive actions need confirmation or undo. Submit is not destructive but it IS irreversible (once submitted, the daily report is locked). The employee who accidentally picked the wrong feeling has no moment to catch it. Norman: "the best error message is one that was never needed" — a pre-submit review prevents the error entirely.
What Employee Experiences: Employee rushes through Act 3. Accidentally picks "Overwhelmed" instead of "Neutral." Hits Submit. Summary shows overwhelmed. Cant change it. Manager sees burnout signal that isnt real. The employees actual feeling was misrepresented because there was no pause to verify.
Fix: Add 2-tap confirm: first tap changes button text to "Confirm?" with btn-warning style. Second tap submits. Auto-revert after 3s if no second tap. Minimal friction, prevents accidents.

Problem: Framework quantity persists when switching selections. Pick Strategy at qty 5, switch to Engineering — qty stays at 5.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman conceptual model: switching to a new framework is a new selection. Carrying over the quantity from a different framework breaks the mental model. "I practiced Code Review 5 times" makes no sense when they only switched from Budget Review (which they did 5 times) to Code Review (which they did once).
What Employee Experiences: Employee picks Strategy > Budget review. Sets quantity to 5. Realizes they meant Engineering > Code Review. Switches macro and micro. Quantity still shows 5. They might not notice. Report says they practiced Code Review 5 times. False data. Or they notice and have to manually fix to 1. Either way: wrong.
Fix: In handleMacroMicroSelect: always reset quantity to 1. onSelect({...s, quantity: 1}). New selection = fresh count.

Problem: startedAt in atom initial value uses Date.now() at module import time, not component mount time. Timer starts before employee opens report.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: If module is imported during app initialization (common with code splitting preloads), startedAt could be minutes or hours before the employee actually starts the report. Timer shows 05:23 on first render. Employee thinks the system is broken.
What Employee Experiences: Employee navigates to daily report. Timer shows 02:15 instead of 00:00. Confusing. "Did I already start this?" Trust erodes on first impression.
Fix: Use lazy initializer in atom or re-initialize startedAt via useEffect on DailyReportV6Inner mount.

Problem: handleConstraintSelect calls setState twice when pairing — once for constraint alone, then again for constraint + navigation. Two renders, potential visual flicker.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Norman feedback: every action should produce ONE perceivable result. Two rapid state updates can cause the navigation section to flash (first render: no nav, second render: highlighted nav). On slow devices this is visible.
What Employee Experiences: Employee picks constraint micro. Navigation section briefly shows no highlight, then highlights the paired macro. Flash. Subtle but undermines the "the system is responding to me" feeling.
Fix: Merge into single setState: set both constraint and paired navigation in one call. One render. Clean transition.

Problem: Unplanned items use Date.now() as ID. Two items added in same millisecond get same ID. React key collision.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Edge case but real on fast double-taps. Duplicate keys cause React reconciliation bugs — second item may not render, or first item gets overwritten.
What Employee Experiences: Employee double-taps Add on unplanned form. Only one item appears. Or items swap/flicker. Rare but disorienting.
Fix: Use crypto.randomUUID() instead of Date.now().

Problem: All animations play regardless of prefers-reduced-motion. Submit button breathes on 2s loop. Pills bounce. Summary slides. WCAG 2.1 concern.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Vestibular disorders affect ~35% of adults over 40. Continuous animation causes dizziness and nausea. The submit button's repeating scale animation is the worst offender — its in the employees peripheral vision while they consider their choice.
What Employee Experiences: Employee with vestibular sensitivity opens report. Constant motion. Feels sick. Closes app. Never returns. The ritual that was supposed to build engagement becomes a medical barrier.
Fix: Import useReducedMotion from framer-motion. When true: all durations to 0, remove repeating animations. Priority files: Act3Close (breathing button), PillSelector (bounce), SummaryCard (checkmark overshoot).

Problem: No role=dialog, no aria-modal, no focus trap, no Escape key handler. Focus escapes behind overlay.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Screen reader users dont know the summary appeared. Keyboard users cant dismiss it. Focus lands behind the overlay on interactive elements they cant see. WCAG 2.1 AA failure.
What Employee Experiences: Screen reader user submits report. Hears nothing about the summary. Tab key moves focus to elements behind the dark overlay. Escape does nothing. They refresh the page to get unstuck.
Fix: Add role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby pointing to Day captured heading. Add onKeyDown for Escape. Add focus trap.

Problem: PillSelector pills are generic buttons. No role=radio, no aria-checked, no radiogroup wrapper. Screen readers announce "button Budget" with no selection state.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: The 5x5 grids ARE the curriculum (Goldratt). If an employee using a screen reader cant interact with the grids properly, they're excluded from the learning. Accessibility is not polish — its access to the curriculum itself.
What Employee Experiences: Screen reader user hears "button Budget, button Talent, button Internal Support..." — no indication which is selected, no group context, no "1 of 5" count. They cant use the grids effectively. The curriculum is locked.
Fix: Wrap in role=radiogroup with aria-label. Each pill: role=radio, aria-checked={isSelected}. Pass aria-label prop from each MacroMicroPicker usage.

Problem: VoiceRecorder and StoryConfirmation textareas have placeholder but no label or aria-label. Screen readers say "edit text."
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: The narrative is vector 5 of 7. If the employee cant identify the input, they cant provide the narrative. Data vector lost for that user.
What Employee Experiences: Screen reader user reaches textarea. Hears "edit text." Edit what? Where? No context. They type something generic or skip. Narrative quality drops. Signal strength: weak.
Fix: Add aria-label="Your narrative" to VoiceRecorder textarea. aria-label="Edit your story" to StoryConfirmation textarea.

Problem: Timer span has no role=timer, no aria-live. Screen readers never announce elapsed time.
Why It Matters (Polya/Gallup/Norman/Gold: Minor but contributes to the sense of "am I in a form or a ritual?" For sighted users the ticking timer creates gentle urgency. For screen reader users: nothing. Different experience = different engagement.
What Employee Experiences: Screen reader user has no sense of time passing. The ritual feels untimed and formless. No cadence.
Fix: Add role=timer, aria-live=polite, aria-label="Elapsed time" to timer span.
